title: Lightweight customer timeline + recovery options
body:
Purpose:
This is a short, customer-facing friendly timeline + choice matrix we can use for fast updates (status page + targeted emails) after inference-quality or latency incidents. The doc is intentionally concise so CS reps can copy/paste and pick options based on customer tier and appetite for remediation.

High-level guidance (POV):
- Keep the public status update tight: what happened, who impacted (broad bucket: hosted/dedicated/private), immediate mitigations, and an ETA for next update.
- Use targeted customer emails for operational choices: do they want a replay/verification bundle, a credit offer, a temporary routing change, or assistance re-instrumenting key prompts?
- For enterprise customers: include an evidence digest (logs + sample requests) and an offer for a short call with engineering within 48 hours.

One-line summary (example to use on status page):
"We experienced increased request latency and occasional degraded responses for some text-generation requests in our hosted eu-west region from 03:14–03:52 UTC on 2026-10-02. Mitigations deployed; routing and normal performance restored by 03:58 UTC. We are investigating and will publish a short customer-facing timeline and options by 2026-10-07."

Suggested short status page template (public):
- Impact: Increased latency and transient degraded outputs affecting customers using hosted generation in eu-west. Not all tenants impacted; Dedicated pools and private deployments were not affected.
- Current status: Services restored; monitoring stable.
- Next steps: Running scoped validation checks and compiling per-tenant impact notes. Expected update: 2026-10-07 17:00 UTC.

Targeted customer email template (choose / edit):
Subject: Incident 2026-10-02 — impact summary and options for {tenant_name}
Hi {customer_ops},

Quick summary: on 2026-10-02 between ~03:14–03:52 UTC some generation requests routed via eu-west experienced intermittent high latency and, in a small fraction of cases, truncated or lower-quality outputs. Our initial remediation (routing and kernel-scale adjustment) restored normal throughput by 03:58 UTC.

What this means for you (short):
- If you saw slow responses only: no replay needed; responses are persisted and consistent.
- If you saw incorrect or truncated outputs: we can offer an integrity review and a small sample replay to verify correctness against model variants.

Choices we can take (pick one):
1) Evidence & verification bundle (free): we provide a short artifact pack (request IDs, timestamps, model variant used, sample outputs) and will re-run a subset of affected requests against the stable model variant to show expected outputs. Good for customers who require proof-of-integrity before accepting resumed traffic.
2) Operational credit (one-off): for customers who prefer a simple financial remediation for developer friction. Typical offers: 1–5% usage credit depending on severity.
3) Temporary routing change: we can route your tenant away from eu-west for up to 72 hours while additional validation completes (note: small latency delta to your end-users may appear).
4) Engineering review session: 30–60 minute call with a solutions engineer to review request traces and prompt-hardening suggestions.

Tell us which option you prefer and we’ll action within 48 hours. If no reply in 7 days we’ll assume you do not want an evidence bundle and will close with a public postmortem link.

Short customer-facing timeline (to include in email or status page link):
- 03:14 UTC — First elevated latency alerts for eu-west generation service.
- 03:20 UTC — On-call performs initial triage; observed increased kernel queueing and edge traffic surge.
- 03:35 UTC — Risk mitigation: shifted traffic away from a subset of overloaded nodes and enabled queued request shedding for low-priority paths.
- 03:48 UTC — Quick patch: adjusted kernel concurrency and restarted affected serving instances.
- 03:52 UTC — Monitoring showed improvement; additional validation in progress.
- 03:58 UTC — Normalized traffic routing and stable latency.
- 04:10 UTC — Post-incident verification checks started (prefix/KV cache sanity, sampling).

Root-cause (customer summary, succinct):
Preliminary root-cause: a combination of an abrupt traffic spike from a noisy tenant plus a latent kernel scheduling regression triggered a backlog in request processing that in a minority of requests led to truncated outputs. The kernel regression surfaced only under a specific sequence length distribution and quantization profile that the affected model used.

Immediate engineering mitigations (customer-level):
- Traffic was temporarily rebalanced across zones.
- Kernel concurrency limits were changed to prevent queue amplification.
- Extra sampling/validation added to CI for sequence-length distributions.

Planned follow-ups (what customers can expect):
- Detailed technical postmortem for customers (short form) by 2026-10-07 with per-tenant impact notes where applicable.
- Permanent kernel fix and a regression test in our build pipeline within the next release window (ETA 2 weeks).
- New synthetic validation for sequence-length/quantization combos to prevent recurrence.

Customer action checklist (copyable):
- If you observed truncated outputs, reply "EVIDENCE" and we’ll prepare the verification bundle.
- If you’d like a call, reply "CALL" with preferred times.
- If you want automatic re-route off eu-west, reply "REROUTE" and confirm the tenant id.

Evidence & verification bundle contents (what to expect):
- Top-level csv of affected request IDs and timestamps (sampled).
- Model variant, sequence-length, and quantization profile for each sample.
- Side-by-side comparison of stored output vs re-run stable variant (text + diff).
- Short integrity statement signed by product/eng lead.

Internal notes / playbook reminders (for CS use):
- Prioritize enterprise customers and any tenants with strict compliance tags.
- Keep language non-technical unless the customer explicitly requests details.
- Avoid promising credits in the first reply; coordinate with finance for >2% credit offers.
- When compiling the evidence bundle, strip any PII and follow data access approvals (see CONFLUENCE-IR-2026-10-02).
- Pull request traces from infra: service:generation-eu-west, timeframe: 2026-10-02 03:10–04:20 UTC, sample rate: 1/10 for heavy tenants.

FAQ quicklines (copy/paste):
Q: Will my data be lost?
A: No — requests and outputs were persisted and remain available. We will include sampled request IDs in the evidence bundle.

Q: Are private deployments affected?
A: No — this was specific to hosted eu-west routing. Customers on Dedicated/Private were not impacted.

Q: How do I get a credit?
A: Reply with "CREDIT" and a CS lead will coordinate the offer and confirm the amount after verifying impact.

Sample closing postmortem summary (short, for public page or customer email):
Title: Brief: eu-west generation latency and truncated outputs (2026-10-02)
Summary: During a ~40-minute window a traffic spike plus a scheduling regression caused increased latency and a small number of truncated outputs. Services were restored through traffic rebalancing and kernel concurrency adjustments. Permanent regression fix and extra validation are in progress.

Appendix (internal):
- TODO: confirm exact percentage of requests that returned truncated outputs; aim to have a per-tenant number before 2026-10-07.
- TODO: draft engineering postmortem and attach test vectors to the customer evidence bundle.
- Question: do we offer an automatic 1% credit for all impacted tenants or only offer on request? Recommend: opt-in by default (customer must request credit) to avoid over-crediting small/no-impact tenants.

Notes to self: Quick rounds with eng (Diego) and product (Samir) scheduled 2026-10-03 morning to finalize per-tenant decisions. Keep this doc short and produce final email templates for VIP and standard tiers.
